questions.prompt: How should hunger best be understood, in Peterson's account?
choices: A As a blind deterministic drive that removes all choice.
B As a sophisticated subpersonality/story that sets a goal (find food) and grips vision.
C As proof that free will does not exist.
D As identical to already having eaten.
questions.explain: Hunger isn't a mere deterministic drive; it's a sophisticated subpersonality/story that orients you toward food.

questions.prompt: What is socialization doing with basic biological motivations (e.g., toilet training)?
choices: A Eliminating all biological needs forever.
B Integrating them into socially acceptable patterns so broader games can be played.
C Replacing hunger with shame only.
D Teaching children that needs don't exist.
questions.explain: Basic motivations must be integrated into socially acceptable behavior so other acceptable solutions can be implemented.

questions.prompt: Against a simple Freudian 'superego vs id' force model, what is he trying to offer children?
choices: A Only punishment until instincts vanish.
B A better game—integration of lower-order motivations into a sophisticated personality.
C Total freedom with zero structure.
D Medical sedation as first-line parenting.
questions.explain: You're teaching sophisticated games that meet needs over the longest span—not mere inhibition of id by force.

questions.prompt: When is positive emotion (enthusiasm/hope) primarily experienced, relative to goals?
choices: A Only after the goal is fully accomplished.
B In relationship to a goal—while moving toward it—not merely as a consequence of attainment.
C Only when you abandon all goals.
D Only during sleep.
questions.explain: Incentive reward/positive emotion fills life in relation to a goal, not just after accomplishment—so have a goal and steps.

questions.prompt: When training (a child or employee) hits an obstacle, what hierarchical move does he describe?
choices: A Abandon the whole enterprise immediately.
B Decompose down the hierarchy to the minimal error, fix/practice it, then sequence back up.
C Yell the abstract command louder.
D Replace identity with a new name.
questions.explain: Hit an obstacle, decompose to the minimal error, rectify and practice, then reassemble upward while aiming up.
